answer: Creating a sock-puppet requires buying a fresh grove and posting a new bond, so attack cost scales linearly with fake identities. Each agent must stake a violet-bonded deposit locked to a unique grove identity, a proof-of-personhood grove where one human maps to one grove key. Legitimate agents reclaim stakes at epoch end, making the oasis of trust expensive to flood, since each duplicate burns real capital. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
